steadfastly

STED-fast-lee · adverb

Hear It

What It Means

Steadfastly is in a firm, loyal, and unwavering manner.

Despite three rejections from investors, she steadfastly believed her invention would eventually change the industry.

Worked Example

Even when the whole town turned against him, the old judge steadfastly refused to change his ruling just to please the crowd.

Holding firm to a position or commitment without wavering, no matter the pressure, is exactly what steadfastly describes.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

doggedly: Doggedly means with stubborn, grinding persistence -- rereading the same file for the hundredth time, refusing to quit long after hope has faded. What drives it is sheer stubbornness. Steadfastly is persistence driven by loyalty and firm belief: you hold on steadfastly because of a commitment, not just because you won't let go.

resolutely: Resolutely means with firm determination, especially at the moment of deciding or acting -- she resolutely shut the door on the offer. Steadfastly stretches that firmness over time: staying loyal and unmoved through months or years of pressure. Resolutely fits a single decisive act; steadfastly fits a long faithful stand.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

halfheartedly: without enthusiasm or full effort

waveringly: in an uncertain, hesitant way that keeps changing

Where it sits · how much loyal resolve drives the persistence — unwaveringly → steadfastly → devotedly

unwaveringly vs. steadfastly: Unwaveringly is milder than steadfastly: keeping a light burning unwaveringly simply means never faltering, while doing it steadfastly goes further, adding fierce loyalty and firm resolve through fifty years of storms.

devotedly vs. steadfastly: Devotedly goes further than steadfastly: a volunteer who steadfastly keeps her weekly shift shows firm, loyal resolve, but nursing one ailing friend devotedly means love itself drives the persistence, beyond any duty or promise.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — stead

root — stead: place, position (Old English)

root — fast

root — fast: firmly fixed, secure (Old English)

suffix — -ly

suffix — -ly: in this manner (adverb ending) (Old English)

Put it together

Put it together: Steadfastly comes from stead ('place, position') plus fast ('firmly fixed') plus the adverb ending -ly, 'in this manner.' To act steadfastly is to stay firmly fixed in your place -- your position, loyalty, or commitment -- no matter what pressure comes.

Use the root in a new word: steady

Use the root in a new word: steady: He kept a steady hand on the wheel even as the road turned icy.

Root Check

Word Choice

Steadfastly describes the manner of persisting over time -- loyalty, belief, or effort that doesn't waver -- rather than a burst of courage in a single dangerous moment, which is closer to what dauntless or plucky describe.
